Dose (S)equence (C)omparison Inconsistent Records

Source: R/sc_inconsistent.R
sc_inconsistent.Rd

This function returns a person-level table of all inconsistent dose sequences (sequences where an earlier dose is skipped, e.g. DTP1 + DTP3, and/or where the doses were not administered in chronological order, e.g. DTP2 before DTP1), in a schedule-like format: one row per person and one column per dose of the sequence, containing the date the dose was administered.

Usage

sc_inconsistent(
  data.EIR,
  vaccines,
  birth_cohorts = NULL,
  allow_same_day = FALSE,
  fix_residence = TRUE
)

Arguments

data.EIR

Data frame. A data frame containing individual vaccination records. See immunABC.EIR for expected structure.

vaccines

Character. A character vector of at least two doses with the ordered dose sequence to evaluate, e.g. c("DTP1", "DTP2", "DTP3").

birth_cohorts

Numeric (optional). A vector specifying the birth cohort(s) for which inconsistent sequences should be returned. If NULL (default), all available cohorts are used.

allow_same_day

Logical. Whether two consecutive doses administered on the same day are considered chronologically consistent. Default is FALSE, since doses of the same vaccine series should not be administered on the same day.

fix_residence

Logical. When a person's residence differs across their records, whether to correct all of that person's records to the residence of their most recent vaccination (TRUE, default) or leave the data as-is (FALSE), in which case each person is assigned the residence of their first record.

Value

A data frame with one row per person with an inconsistent sequence, with the following columns:

  • ID: unique person identification number.

  • date_birth: date of birth.

  • ADM1_residence, ADM2_residence: place of residence.

  • One column per dose in vaccines, in the order of the sequence: the date the dose was administered (the earliest one, if duplicated), or NA if it was not received (or was received with no date_vax).

  • sequence: the combination of doses received, e.g. "DTP1 + DTP3".

  • skipped_doses: the doses of the sequence skipped, i.e. not received but followed by a dose that was received, e.g. "DTP2" for "DTP1 + DTP3". NA if no dose was skipped.

  • out_of_order: whether the doses received were not administered in chronological order.

Details

Only people with at least one dose of the sequence are evaluated. Since this is a nominal indicator, each person is assigned to a single place of residence (see fix_residence).
